provenance: Conventions specific to dating-app profiles and early-stage messaging, where emoji do compressed disclosure work: a bio has severe space limits, so single glyphs stand for orientation, intent, lifestyle and dealbreakers. Widely documented in app-culture journalism and in the apps' own prompt design.

📍.gloss: Almost universal bio opener: pin followed by a city. Rarely a literal map reference.

📏.gloss: The ruler prefixes a height, a disclosure convention that emerged because height filtering is so contested.

🎓.gloss: Signals a degree or institution as a compressed status claim.

💼.gloss: Prefixes a job title in the same bio grammar.

♑.gloss: Zodiac glyphs in bios are a genuine filtering mechanism for a substantial share of users, and a joke for the rest. All twelve function identically.

🧿.gloss: Reads as an interest in astrology, energy and manifestation.

✈️.gloss: The single most parodied bio emoji, to the point where using it sincerely now reads as self-aware.

🐕.gloss: Pet ownership is a stated dealbreaker often enough to warrant its own glyph.

🐈.gloss: The counterpart claim, and a mild tribal signal.

🚭.gloss: Compact statement of a lifestyle boundary.

🚫🍷.gloss: Sobriety disclosure, increasingly common as a positive claim rather than an apology.

🌱.gloss: Dietary disclosure, and by implication a values claim.

♀️.gloss: Paired gender symbols in a bio state who the user is looking for, more precisely than app filters allow.

🏳️‍🌈.gloss: In a dating bio specifically this reads as a statement about the user, unlike its use on corporate accounts.

💜.sense: demisexual or ace-spectrum, in some communities
💜.gloss: Colour-coded orientation signalling varies by platform and cohort; unreliable but real.

♠️.gloss: The ace of spades as an established ace-community identity marker.

🤍.gloss: Intent signalling; contrasted deliberately with the more casual hearts.

🔥.gloss: The most common compliment token in early messaging.

👀.gloss: Low-risk expression of attention, deniable if unreciprocated.

🥺.gloss: Used to make a request hard to refuse; frequently read as manipulative.

😏.gloss: The standard marker that a conversation is changing register.

🙈.gloss: Softens a confession or a bold suggestion.

😅.gloss: Deployed after a message lands badly.

👻.gloss: Naming the practice of vanishing mid-conversation; the app-culture term is now more common than the spectre.

🍞.gloss: Stringing someone along with intermittent low-effort contact.

🧊.gloss: Deliberate cooling of contact, a step short of ghosting.

🚩.gloss: The dominant dating-discourse glyph, used both in bios ('no red flags please') and in post-date debriefs with friends.

🟢.gloss: The deliberate inversion of 🚩, marking a positive trait. A newer coinage that spread because the negative had become so dominant.

💔.gloss: Used for relationships that never had a formal status to end.

🫠.gloss: Burnout from swiping, a genre of post in its own right.

🛌.gloss: Signals casual rather than serious intent when placed in a bio.

🌚.gloss: Implies the conversation is heading somewhere without saying so.

🧢.gloss: Applied to implausible bio claims, especially heights.

📸.gloss: Asking for proof the person is real, in a catfishing-aware culture.
